items.title: Benny Golson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Gil Evans hired him to do a session with him

ctx.x: When you say that – you grew up in Philly, and you played with Philly Joe Jones. What is it specifically about Art Blakey’s drums?

Whew. His – have you ever heard people say a piano player had a good touch, a certain touch? A drummer can have a certain touch. When Art Blakey sat down – I don’t care whose drums it was – it sounded like Art Blakey. It sounded like him. You could turn your head, I could hear a recording, I know it’s him. It’s just something about him, about that cymbal. Somebody could sit down and play his drums, but when he sits down, it sounds different. It’s that thing that reaches in and touches. It touched my heart. That’s…
Are we going to end? Because I – when we pick up, I’m going to ask you where you got all your business acumen that you passed on Bu?
